messages:
Sam: Customer reports their monthly token bucket dropped to 0 right after midnight UTC and they got a stream of 429s. They claim they bought a one-off top-up at 23:58 and UI showed credit but API returned 429s. Can we triage?
Maya (CS): Acked. Customer is acme-inc-prod. They saw UI show +10k credits at 23:58, then UI back to 0 around 00:01; API 429s started at 00:00:20. They pasted a few logs.
Ida (Billing): I pulled the billing ledger for acme-inc-prod. There is a plan change (upgrade) at 23:57:43 that created a prorated credit entry and a manual topup at 23:58:12. Both entries exist in the ledger. No refunds or reversals.
Kevin (Infra): I checked the refill job and cache invalidation. Refill job ran at 00:00:00 UTC and wrote new balance for tenant id t-54321. However our tenant-visible cache key (tenant_balance:v1:t-54321) had a TTL of 5m and was last refreshed at 23:58:05. Refill wrote to DB but failed a cache delete step due to a transient redis timeout (timeout logged 00:00:01). That left the old cached zero visible to API nodes for ~4m until TTL expired.
Sam: That matches the visible symptom: UI initially showed topup (because frontend read DB?), then after a quick refresh UI showed 0. Customer says their long-poll websocket stayed connected and continued to retry, resulting in many small consumption events. Do retries count?
Kevin (Infra): Yes — each streaming chunk that finishes and is billed increments usage. We saw a retry storm between 00:00:20 and 00:02:00 from acme's IPs: ~3500 requests with exponential backoff misconfigured (tight 200ms cap). Many of those were accepted by some nodes that read DB directly (not cache) after the refill completed, so tokens were used down to zero.
Maya (CS): Customer says client retrier believes request failed due to 429 and keeps retrying until UI shows credit. They were on an old SDK version that retries aggressively.
Ida (Billing): Ledger shows consumption entries from 00:00:20 onwards that sum to the topup amount and then further, so it's not a billing calculation bug — it was consumed. We can provide transaction IDs.
Sam: Customer wants to understand why UI showed credit then 0 and why the API 429 happened immediately after refill. Root cause seems to be cache invalidation race + aggressive client retries consuming the refill quickly.
Kevin (Infra): Repro steps I used:
```
# simulate tenant with cached zero
# 1) set cache to 0 with long TTL
redis-cli set tenant_balance:v1:t-54321 0 EX 300
# 2) write topup to DB (simulate refill job)
psql -c "INSERT INTO tenant_balances ..."
# 3) hit refill code path which tries to DEL cache then write DB. If DEL fails, cache remains 0.
# 4) run a tight retrier loop against /v1/generate to show consumption:
for i in {1..2000}; do curl -sS -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED\" \"https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate\" -d '{\"prompt\":\"hi\"}' & done
```
Response sample we saw from customer: 
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
X-RateLimit-Limit: 120000
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 1718769000
X-Credits-Visible: 0
{"error":{"message":"quota exhausted"}}
```
Ida (Billing): Actionable for billing: we can issue a one-time safety topup and mark as goodwill while infra fixes the race. Transaction metadata available on request.
Sam: Suggested immediate mitigation: issue a small emergency topup so customer can recover, ask them to pause their load for 10 min, and provide guidance to update SDK to non-aggressive retries.
Maya (CS): I told the customer to pause and we applied a +15k emergency topup at 01:02 UTC. Customer confirmed they could call API again. They updated SDK and backed off.
Kevin (Infra): For root fix: I'll open a PR to make refill job atomic with a strong cache delete-and-check loop and add a short leader lock so only one refill runs per tenant. Also will add a metric/alert for refill job cache-delete failures.
Sam: Also recommend we add server-side protection: at refill time temporarily throttle inbound requests for that tenant for 30s to avoid immediate consumption storms.
Ida (Billing): Follow-ups: file a refund/goodwill memo if needed. I'll prepare the reconciliation report for finance.
DeployBot: deploy queued: patch/atomic-refill v1 -> staging at 09:20, will promote pending verification.
Sam: Thanks all. I'll close the support ticket once infra confirms patch and we verify no other tenants hit the race.
Kevin (Infra): Note: we should also add a UX signal to show \"recent refill in progress\" in Console so customers know to hold retries for 60s.
Maya (CS): I'll follow up with customer in 24h to confirm no recurrence. :thumbsup:
Sam: Closing notes for thread: root cause = cache invalidation race during refill + aggressive client retries consuming tokens. Remediation = emergency topup + patch atomic refill + client guidance.
